source.title: Over Parameterized Two-level Neural Networks Can Learn Near Optimal Feature Representations
source.authors: Cong Fang; Hanze Dong; Tong Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Compares random and learned-feature initializations during training and reports that the learned-feature initialization has lower training loss in every epoch. This bears conceptually on initialization and training speed, but does not test the specific activation-matched or orthogonal initializations in V4.
record.gate_note: The main experiments report test error and training-loss curves for feature repopulation. Training loss does not establish the training classification error named in V1. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study investigates learned feature distributions and their sampling efficiency. Its initialization comparison uses task-learned features versus Gaussian weights; it does not test V4's activation-matched signal and gradient preservation mechanism. Its other results do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under stated assumptions, continuous infinite-width noisy gradient dynamics converge to a regularized optimum whose feature distribution is near optimal for sampling efficiency under suitable regularization. Experiments report advantages for learned or generated features over task-independent random features.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments compare Gaussian random initialization with initialization from a learned feature distribution; they do not use the activation-matched or orthogonal initialization recipes in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization choice changes the reported training-loss trajectory: generated-feature initialization is described as having lower training loss at every epoch than Gaussian initialization on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D.4 reports lower training loss at every epoch with generated-feature initialization than with Gaussian initialization in 100-hidden-node two-layer networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization from a task-learned feature distribution can improve subsequent training-loss trajectories relative to Gaussian initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 establishes asymptotic convergence of continuous noisy gradient dynamics to the regularized global optimum under stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Infinite-width two-layer networks can converge to a regularized global optimum under suitable smoothness, initialization, and noise assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.4 explains normalization through reduced feature-sampling variance; Appendix D.2 uses normalization to compare feature efficiency without a normalization ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalizing feature second moments can improve sampling efficiency when approximating a learned target function.

record.problems: The relevant training-loss values are presented only in plots; the text gives a qualitative comparison. These experiments use a specific two-layer feedforward setup with 100 hidden nodes and do not test the initialization schemes specifically named in V4.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows included. Other training-loss and test-error curves concern feature repopulation or importance sampling and do not test the initialization claim in V4 as mapped here.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima in finite-width ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients, its effects on learning speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth and recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: Lower training loss alone does not establish V1's training classification error. Infinite-width convergence does not establish V2's finite-width teacher-student result. The normalization argument concerns representation efficiency rather than V6's acceleration or learning-rate tolerance.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error from random initialization, including on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 with corrupted or random labels; model size, training duration, early stopping and regularization effects.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects, identity shortcuts, special initialization of plain deep networks, and residual networks without normalization.
Activation-matched and signal-preserving initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and training plain networks at 10,000 layers.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises and recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: Gaussian initialization (Random)
rows.operation_detail: Train both layers from Gaussian random initialization; compare training loss across epochs with generated-feature initialization.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars represent standard deviation; values not stated.
rows.note: The authors state that the generated initialization has smaller training loss in every epoch; precise values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Figure 10 reports lower training loss with generated features on MNIST, but neither tests activation-matched initialization nor measures signal preservation or trainable depth. This is a comparator for the study's own method; 'partial' incorrectly implies an incomplete V4 effect.
